comments.body:
Research: mutation testing in active OSS CI (2026-08-10)

Operator direction is supported, with one terminology correction: mutmut mutates production code, not new/modified test files. Changed tests should trigger the narrow production shard they cover, and that shard should run using the relevant tests.

Observed maintained-project patterns:
- PostHog/posthog-python runs a targeted mutation job on PRs/main only when one named production file or either of its paired test files changed. It uses one Python version, a normal pytest timeout, max-children=1, and a cache key hashing the source and tests; an exact cache hit skips the run. New survivors hard-fail. Source: https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-python/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
- 567-labs/instructor keeps mutation manual and targets one async-retry function family. It caps the job at 30 minutes, max-children=4, pins mutmut==3.6.0, runs from a clean git archive, and enforces explicit budgets for known structural survivors and one known infinite-loop timeout rather than requiring a misleading perfect score. Source: https://github.com/567-labs/instructor/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
- Trail of Bits trailmark runs its small full mutation suite on PR/main, cancels superseded runs, and always prints results. Source: https://github.com/trailofbits/trailmark/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
- GeoParquet runs the broad suite nightly/manual with a hard job timeout. It retries only transient DuckDB-extension installation, treats mutmut execution failure as failure, treats zero generated/parsed mutants as a hard failure, compares against a checked-in score floor, and always uploads artifacts. Source: https://github.com/geoparquet/geoparquet-io/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml

Official mutmut guidance confirms two cache hazards and mitigations: result-affecting config changes invalidate cache automatically; non-Python dependency/config changes need watched files and on_dependency_change=rerun to avoid stale results. Its per-mutant timeout is derived from baseline test duration plus a constant times a multiplier. Source: https://mutmut.readthedocs.io/en/latest/#detecting-dependency-and-config-changes and #unstable-configs

Recommended rebar design: in Gerrit Validate, detect newly added/modified tests, map them to an existing selected behavioral-core shard (or the directly covered source functions), run the normal shard once as a baseline, then run only those mutants with a pinned Python/mutmut version, low bounded concurrency, and per-mutant plus whole-job timeouts. Cache only on an exact hash of production source + selected tests + lock/config inputs. A zero-mutant run, baseline-test failure, tool crash, timeout-budget overrun, new survivor, or score regression must be distinguishable in output. Do not blanket-retry mutation outcomes; retry only independently identified infrastructure setup failures. Keep the broader baseline sweep scheduled/manual.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Mutation testing should protect changed behavioral cores, but the historical whole-file counts are stale. A pinned mutmut 3.7.0 probe found 814 mutants in `signing.py` versus 491 in the old record, including both equivalent survivors and real contract gaps. Enforcing the old ceilings would block unrelated work; accepting all current survivors would normalize defects. The approved rollout therefore starts with evidence gathering and promotes each shard only when its results and runtime justify stronger enforcement.

## Plan

Use `.github/mutation-shards.toml` as the sole source for shard mappings, reviewed equivalent fingerprints, explicit timeout inputs, and an explicit per-shard enforcement mode:

- `advisory`: run head mutation evidence and publish every outcome. Existing survivors, `no tests`, and timeouts are nonblocking mutation-quality findings. Missing, zero-mutant, incomplete, or unrecognized evidence blocks, as do configuration, selection, execution, and artifact-contract failures, because usable evidence was not produced.
- `ratchet`: compare fresh base/head archives. For AST-identical functions, preserve unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` outcomes. Block killed mutants that disappear or become survived, timed out, incomplete, or `no tests`; block new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses. Report newly introduced `no tests` without blocking because mutmut cannot reliably attribute subprocess tests. Added or edited functions must kill every mutant unless a survivor matches an individually reviewed equivalent fingerprint; `no tests` remains report-only in ratchet.
- `strict`: apply the changed-function rule to the entire shard. Every mutant must be killed or individually fingerprinted as equivalent; `no tests`, timeouts, incomplete statuses, and zero mutants block. Strict promotion therefore requires direct in-process mutation coverage.

Start all legacy shards as advisory. Promote a shard to ratchet only after three successful base/head pilot runs show stable mappings and a maximum runtime of 24 minutes or less inside its 30-minute job. If a shard cannot meet that threshold, narrow it to proven function patterns before promotion. Promote it to strict only after legacy non-killed outcomes are remediated or individually reviewed. Mode changes are small manifest reviews; there is no fuzzy severity classification.

A selector inspects `HEAD^..HEAD`, including both sides of renames. Mapped source, test, or support changes select their shards; mutation-infrastructure changes select all. Unmapped changed Python tests are reported as advisory findings. Unresolved refs or diffs fail; an empty selection is an explicit successful skip. The reusable workflow emits selector JSON and creates one matrix job per selected shard, so every shard has its own 30-minute cap. Advisory evaluates head only; ratchet evaluates fresh base and head archives; strict evaluates complete head evidence plus the regression evidence required by the driver.

For each archive the driver synthesizes `[tool.mutmut]` from the canonical manifest before execution. The repository does not retain a second global `[tool.mutmut]` shard mapping. The manifest pins `timeout_constant = 1.0` and `timeout_multiplier = 15.0`; mutmut therefore gives each mutant a wall limit of `(estimated selected-test runtime + 1 second) * 15`, while the workflow independently caps the shard job at 30 minutes. Each job uses Python 3.12, pinned `mutmut==3.7.0`, `--max-children 1`, and selected clean-test preflight. Dependency downloads may be cached; mutation verdict state may not. Gerrit checks out the exact patchset and includes mutation in `vote.needs`; the push/PR lane mirrors it. A weekly/manual sweep selects every shard through the same selector and matrix.

Mutation-result reruns are diagnostic only and cannot turn red green. Only independently identified setup failures may retry. Raw logs, survivor diffs and fingerprints, and a structured summary publish for every driver outcome. Documentation describes the live manifest policy and promotion process and removes stale score or budget tables. A contract test reads the documentation, asserts the required policy sections and mode names, and asserts the historical score-table heading is absent. The existing two-vote rollback runbook remains the emergency recovery path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Selection maps changed source, test, support, and global inputs to the expected shard set.
- [x] Selection keeps both sides of renames and deletions, reports unmatched Python tests, returns an explicit empty selection, fails unresolved refs, and emits selector JSON for targeted or all-shard runs.
- [x] Manifest loading accepts only `advisory`, `ratchet`, or `strict`, emits the pinned timeout values into each archive config, and no duplicate repository mutmut mapping remains.
- [x] Advisory returns success for survived, `no tests`, and timeout mutation-quality findings while returning failure for missing, zero-mutant, incomplete, or unrecognized evidence and configuration or execution errors.
- [x] Ratchet preserves unchanged legacy survivors and `no tests` and reports newly introduced `no tests` without blocking.
- [x] Ratchet blocks killed regressions, missing killed mutants, new survivors, timeouts, and incomplete statuses; added or edited functions require killed mutants or individually reviewed equivalent fingerprints except that `no tests` is report-only.
- [x] Strict requires every mutant to be killed or individually fingerprinted and blocks every `no tests`, timeout, incomplete status, and zero-mutant run.
- [x] Execution uses fresh archives, restores no verdict cache, pins runtime and concurrency, runs clean-test preflight, generates archive-local config, and always writes structured evidence.
- [x] Workflows use selector-derived per-shard matrix jobs with a 30-minute limit each, exact Gerrit patchset checkout, `vote.needs`, push/PR parity, weekly/manual all-shard selection, cancellation, and always-published artifacts.
- [x] A real compact-policy smoke run passes from fresh base/head archives.
- [x] The documentation contract test proves the phased modes, deterministic promotion evidence, false-positive policy, cadence, manifest authority, and absence of stale score or budget tables.

## Verification

    pytest -q tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py
    python scripts/mutation_gate.py smoke --shard compact-policy --base HEAD^ --head HEAD
    python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py
    make config-check
    make lint
    make typecheck

## Primary evidence

Current primary-source examples: Instructor uses a pinned bounded shard with explicit exceptions; DataDog maps changed tests to source and compares base/head; PostHog gates a targeted PR shard; Trailmark cancels superseded runs and always reports; GeoParquet schedules broad mutation, fails on missing evidence, retries setup only, and publishes artifacts. The pinned mutmut 3.7.0 probe verifies `run --help` exposes `--max-children`; `configuration.py` defaults and fingerprints `timeout_constant=1.0` and `timeout_multiplier=15.0`; `__main__.py` derives the wall limit from those values, maps exit codes to every consumed status, and produces survivor output with `difflib.unified_diff`. The real repository probe and corrections are recorded in concise ticket comments.
